rows.TEXT: Yes, you look like one worthy of my magic.
Elves? Buy quick! They kill me if they see you!

Known in his times as the mightiest of all adepts of the black art, this lord was slain by the inquisitor Vorgel who ended his reign of terror. He is now resurrected as an undead with the intention to subjugate every mortal to his will.

Tora'ach 
"Hah! Mindless beast. You want food, do you?"

Illumielle 
"Enough! This is not a game, Tora'ach. I won't have you putting our people at risk."

Tora'ach 
"Have you forgotten who we are, my Queen? We are creatures of the forest, predators to everything within it. Are you too busy decorating your throne room to remember your heritage?"

Illumielle 
"It is because of our heritage that I tolerate you, but my patience has limits. The Elves have more noble tasks than playing with corpses. Destroy this creature and we shall discuss them."

Tora'ach 
"You heard her. Kill it. We've grown bored anyway."

Oracle 
"My Queen, at dawn I was overtaken by a vision! I walked amidst fields of fallen soldiers - Elf, Human, and Dwarf. A fortress loomed over the battlefield, shrouded by fog. Behind me, another army approached, but they were also dead."

Illumielle 
"What? We've received no visions from Gallean in years! How can this be?"

Tora'ach 
"Perhaps this witch has indulged in too much drink! Gallean no longer concerns himself with the mortal world."

Oracle 
"Nonsense. He...they...I can't be sure, but I sensed the presence of two messengers...one standing behind the other. The first warned me of a division within our people, one eating our strength from inside..."

Oracle 
"The other figure, concealed by the fog, told me we must begin to reclaim our forests...that our people will perish should we continue our ways of isolation. He said intruders are planning an invasion, far west of here...he urged us to arms."

Illumielle 
"Gallean...oh, great Gallean. He has returned, then! We must move immediately! Let us equip our forces and move upon our enemies. Oracle, get some rest. You are divinely favored. I'll wager we'll need your gift again before this is done."

Tora'ach 
"Did I hear you correctly? Our Queen moving us to battle? Aye! Perhaps there is hope for our people yet! I will notify the inhabitants of the woods that they are needed at once!"
Conquer the invader city, Hemwyk Court.

Tora'ach 
"No! The graves of our ancestors...they've taken the bodies! See this? This is what happens when your leaders spend their time plotting treaties instead of protecting their lands! No longer!"

Illumielle 
"You speak with a treasonous tongue, Tora'ach! Still, this worries me...Mortis and her armies seldom bother with our dead. We will post sentinels throughout our grave sites. This will not happen again."

Scout 
"This area emanates with power, yes, but can you smell the blood upon the air?"

Oracle 
"Listen...the howling - but not a wolf! One of Mortis' beasts must hunt here. We will not be able to slay it with ordinary weapons! We will need to bring mages to deal with these creatures!"

Fyrwenn 
"I realize most of you have never traveled this far from Hearth's Grove. We move forward by the will of Gallean. He will protect us, but we must still be cautious. This territory is infested by Orcs."
"The Orcs slaughtered the Humans who used to live here. However, I fear they are about to lose their dominion over these woods."

Orc 
"Elves! Elves! Get cyclops! Bring cyclops! Hurry!"

Oracle 
"By Gallean, what is that?!! It's wounded...they've been torturing it!"

Tora'ach 
"Strange...there are humans here. Slaves. I'm surprised the beasts didn't eat them all, though from the looks of it they did bite a few. Make their deaths swift, there is no need to be cruel."

Fyrwenn 
"Do not touch them! Before we lost contact with the Empire, we had an alliance. We owe the humans a great deal.  Set them free. Now."

Tora'ach 
"Humans...free in our forest. I don't see how this benefits us."

Illumielle 
"We should seek aid from the Elves guarding Lachla'an's tomb to the south. They blame us for his death, but we still serve the same god, don't we?  Surely some of them will want to be a part of our march."

Tora'ach 
"Why would we seek their help? They spend their lives mourning the death of a simple magician. Lachla'an was no figure worth worship."

Illumielle 
"Had you been there, Tora'ach, you would have witnessed his miracles with your own eyes. There is no question that he was Gallean's son...what Mortis did to him was...unspeakable."

Fyrwenn 
"Illumielle, I beg of you...remain here. I would be honored to go in your place. We cannot bear to lose another Queen!"

Illumielle 
"Very well, cousin. Tora'ach, you are to listen to her guidance, and I do expect you to return her to me when this is done."

Tora'ach 
"Oh...gladly I would take an arrow to the heart before allowing a relation of our...ruler...any harm."

Elf Lord 
"What's this? An army marches into a graveyard? You are not welcome here. This is a place of mourning."

Tora'ach 
"We come by orders of Gallean! We are preparing for an invasion. We seek any Elves you can spare for our army!"

Elf Lord 
"I think not...Gallean no longer speaks to us. I'm not sure what delusions you are under, but you have no business here. If Gallean truly does favor you as you claim, perhaps he will allow you to visit Lachla'an's original grave to the north."

Elf Lord 
"Perhaps our mighty god will allow you to bring back our avatar's body to seal away in his tomb.  More likely, though, you'll feed the spiders that guard the "nest." Leave. You'll find us far less hospitable than the spiders."

Tora'ach 
"Or...we could just kill these traitors."

Tora'ach 
"We're here. I think I see a bundle down there; these must be the remains they are looking for. Let me just...agggggh...I can't move! I can't will myself to reach it!"

Fyrwenn 
"That doesn't surprise me in the least. Allow me to try. I'm sure Gallean favors those with more righteou...no...I can't...this is not going to work."

Elf Lord 
"Impossible...yet...Gallean be praised! Lachla'an may finally rest! Quickly, take it to the tomb beneath the windmill!"

Elf Lord 
"You will not survive this."

Tora'ach 
"Something that should have been done a long time ago."

Oracle 
"We've been deceived! We can't fight this many!"

Tora'ach 
"Look! The Undead have built a massive city here! The vision was true! They must be planning an invasion..."

Oracle 
"No...that's not right...I mean, yes, they are certainly here, but Gallean...isn't interested in them. We've seen the remnants of her armies for years and had no problem fending them off. We seek something else...to the north."

Tora'ach 
"They have been somewhat less than organized in their attacks, but we will return to deal with them soon! We cannot allow their numbers to grow."

Oracle 
"Yes! We near the city in my visions. We must prepare for battle!"

Peasant 
"Welcome, Elves! What brings you to Hemwyk Court? We haven't seen your kind in years!"
"There must be some mistake. This is a Human village. We have no conflict with the Humans."

Oracle Elf 
"It is...his will. No, it can't be right...Gallean would nev...KILL THEM! KILL THEM NOW!"

Fyrwenn 
"This is insanity! Why do we attack humans?"

Oracle 
"It is his will, as I said. Who are we to question our father?"

Tora'ach 
"Did you not hear his voice? He protects us! He is giving us back our forests! This is a glorious day! To the city!"

Fyrwenn 
"Explain yourself, oracle! This does not feel like the will of Gallean!"

Oracle 
"Without a doubt...they...it...is Gallean. He speaks strangely at times, but it is the same Gallean who spoke to us through Lachla'an. I can feel it. His thoughts are...erratic. He contradicts himself."

Oracle 
"Both of his voices spoke as one...thunderous...urging us to battle. It is why I shouted, or rather, he shouted through me."

Fyrwenn 
"There will be repercussions when the Empire finds out what we have done here. Certainly Gallean has his reasons, but we will need to discover them soon if we are to avoid war."

Oracle 
"I thought this was a simple spider's nest, but look at them...they are weakened because they are close to the pit...yet still they are drawn to it. These two may be a lot less trouble than the rest of their kind."
